blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, the tax calendar is no longer a list of deadlines — it is the rhythm that sets the pace for a large part of the finance function. The months between filings are not 'time off'; they are preparation windows, each with its own small, steady work. The months of filings are not 'crunch time'; they are the visible part of work that has been underway for weeks.

A well-designed calendar gives the team predictability, and predictability lets the team do deeper work: closer reviews, earlier reconciliations, more honest conversations about borderline positions before they harden into filed returns.

What looks from the outside like a routine of quiet, repeated dates is, on the inside, the pattern that holds the whole year together. Remove it, and the finance function turns into a series of emergencies. Protect it, and the emergencies simply stop happening. That is the real product of a calendar, carefully kept, across years of patient executive leadership.

items.q: According to the text, what is the tax calendar at executive level?
options: A checklist owned by the compliance team
A list of deadlines and nothing more
The rhythm that sets the pace for much of the finance function
items.why: "it is the rhythm that sets the pace for a large part of the finance function" — deixa explicitamente de ser mera lista de prazos.

items.q: What does predictability allow the team to do?
options: Work fewer hours during filing months
Do deeper work — closer reviews, earlier reconciliations, more honest conversations
items.why: "predictability lets the team do deeper work: closer reviews, earlier reconciliations…"

items.q: The author suggests that the months between filings are…
options: preparation windows with their own steady work
the period when errors are most likely
items.why: "they are preparation windows, each with its own small, steady work" — não são folga.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The visible filing months rest on invisible earlier work.
Predictability is a precondition for deeper technical work.
Filing season is essentially crunch time that cannot be planned away.
A well-kept calendar prevents recurring emergencies.
items.why: Inferência: o texto rejeita a ideia de 'crunch time' — a temporada de entregas é a parte visível de um trabalho já em curso há semanas.

items.q: The closing contrast "Remove it… Protect it…" suggests that…
options: emergencies are unavoidable in tax functions
the calendar is what silently keeps emergencies from arising
the calendar's value is mostly symbolic
protecting the calendar is optional once systems mature
items.why: Inferência: a estrutura antitética mostra que o próprio ato de proteger o calendário é o que impede as emergências de acontecerem.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily defendendo a rotina do calendário durante um trimestre caótico. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
I know how this looks. We're three weeks into the messiest quarter we've had in years, and here I am insisting we keep the Monday review in the diary — same hour, same room, no exceptions. Two of you have quietly asked whether we might drop it 'just until things settle down'.

Here's my answer. We do not cancel the review because the quarter is hard. We keep the review precisely because the quarter is hard. The moment we let the calendar slip is the moment the chaos stops being visible and starts moving in quietly, position by position, until nobody can say what's actually been filed.

So on Monday we sit down, we walk the reconciliations, and we surface the borderline items now — while they're still soft — rather than a fortnight from now when they've hardened into something we can't reopen.

This is not me being rigid for the sake of it. Protect the rhythm and the emergencies simply stop happening. Let it go, and I promise you, we spend the next two quarters cleaning up after a mess we could have seen coming. Same hour, same room. See you Monday.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What are two of the team members quietly asking Emily to do?
options: Drop the Monday review until things settle down
Move the review to a larger room
Bring in extra staff for the quarter
items.why: "Two of you have quietly asked whether we might drop it 'just until things settle down'."

items.q: What is Emily's core reasoning for keeping the review?
options: They keep the review precisely because the quarter is hard
The board has mandated weekly meetings
It is the only time the team is all available
Cancelling would look bad to auditors
items.why: "We keep the review precisely because the quarter is hard."

items.q: Why does Emily want to surface the borderline items on Monday?
options: To assign blame before the close
While they are still soft, before they harden into something that can't be reopened
items.why: "surface the borderline items now — while they're still soft — rather than… when they've hardened into something we can't reopen."

items.q: What does Emily imply will happen if the calendar slips?
options: The chaos becomes invisible and embeds itself position by position
The review will be reinstated automatically
The team will simply work longer hours
items.why: Inferência: 'the chaos stops being visible and starts moving in quietly' — o risco é o caos deixar de ser visível e se instalar sorrateiramente.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's stance?
options: Disciplined and preventative, protecting a routine on purpose
items.why: Inferência: ela mesma nega rigidez vazia ('This is not me being rigid for the sake of it') — a disciplina é deliberada e preventiva.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The filing schedule gives the whole function a steady rhythm." Here rhythm means…
options: a recurring, predictable pattern of work
items.why: Rhythm = ritmo: o padrão recorrente e previsível que organiza o trabalho ao longo do ano.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The weeks before a filing are a ___ — quiet, but where the real work is done."
items.why: Preparation window = janela de preparação: o período tranquilo em que o trabalho de fato acontece.

items.q: "We flag borderline positions early, before they harden into filed returns." To harden here means to…
options: become fixed and difficult to revisit
items.why: To harden = endurecer: a posição se fixa e deixa de ser fácil de reabrir.

items.q: Predictability, as used in the lesson, is valuable chiefly because it…
options: frees the team to do deeper, earlier work
items.why: Previsibilidade libera a equipe para revisões mais profundas e reconciliações mais cedo — não é um fim em si.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Once the calendar is abandoned, the function turns into a series of ___."
items.why: Emergency = emergência: sem o calendário, o trabalho vira uma sucessão de incêndios a apagar.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs de negócios ligados ao tema. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the year-end positions." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "The team agreed the reconciliation plan but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "Tightening the Monday review won't move the needle unless the data arrives on time." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; sem os dados a tempo, não move o ponteiro.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on keeping the review during the busy quarter." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Let's get ahead of the borderline positions before filing season." To get ahead of something means to…
options: deal with it before it becomes a problem
items.why: Get ahead of = antecipar-se, tratar da questão antes que ela vire um problema.
